units.summary: New helper that reports s.ooo == nil, pulled out of the inline OOO check that used to sit in staleSeriesRefsNoOOOData. Callers use it as a filter and eviction predicate. All callers in the PR hold the series lock.
units.headline: Extract OOO-free check into isSeriesWithoutOOO helper
units.reason: Same condition as the old inline check, now in a helper; it is trivially equivalent.

units.summary: Helper that checks whether lastValue, lastHistogramValue.Sum or lastFloatHistogramValue.Sum is a stale NaN. It is the same expression that was removed from gcStaleSeries and the stale-ref filter. It is now also used to count how many stale series get deleted, which feeds the numStaleSeries gauge.
units.headline: Extract stale-NaN last-sample check into isStaleSeries helper
units.reason: Copied verbatim from the removed inline checks.

units.summary: Now a thin wrapper over truncateSeries. Its predicate requires the series to have no OOO data, to still be stale, and to have no append IDs above the watermark. The OOO check and the append-ID check are new eviction conditions on the existing stale-head compaction path, so this path now evicts fewer series.

issues.title: Watermark misses appenders opened before capture but committed later
issues.failure_scenario: An appender is created (and gets its appendID) before compactHeadViewLocked reads lastAppendID. It commits a sample with ts <= maxt after the block is written. The sample's appendID is <= the watermark, so the guard misses it and the series is evicted with a WAL tombstone, losing the sample. For stale series, isStaleSeries usually catches this unless the late sample is itself a stale marker.

units.headline: Stale truncation now also skips OOO and post-watermark series
units.reason: Changes which series get evicted from the head and tombstoned in the WAL.
focus: The watermark is the last assigned appendID, so appenders that are still open but got their ID earlier are not covered
Whether the new OOO check changes stale-compaction outcomes that tests expect

units.summary: New eviction entry point for CompactSelectedSeries. It evicts any listed series whose maxTime is <= maxt, that has no OOO data and no appendID above the watermark. There is no staleness requirement, so the append-ID watermark is the only guard against losing samples committed during the block write.

issues.title: Late commit from a pre-watermark appender gets evicted and tombstoned
issues.failure_scenario: newAppendID runs when the appender is created (head_test asserts the low watermark advances before commit). An appender opened before `appendIDWatermark := db.head.iso.lastAppendID()` can commit a sample with ts <= maxt after the block write. The sample's appendID is <= the watermark, so the series is evicted and the WAL tombstone drops the sample on replay, and it is not in the block either. This is permanent data loss.

units.headline: New truncation path evicts caller-selected series using an appendID guard
units.reason: New eviction logic that deletes series and writes WAL tombstones; it can lose data if the guard is wrong.
focus: Whether the watermark should be the next ID to be assigned, or should wait for open appenders (lowestAppendTime / appendsOpen)
With isolation disabled the guard is a no-op; check that callers really guarantee no concurrent writes
numStaleSeries is decremented only for evicted series that are stale

units.summary: Walks the series' txRing and returns true if any tracked appendID is greater than the watermark. Returns false when s.txs is nil, which only happens when isolation is disabled (newMemSeries). I checked the absolute claim about disabled isolation against newMemSeries and it holds. The ring keeps the latest append's ID, so a post-watermark append is always detected.
units.headline: Add txRing scan detecting appends newer than a watermark
units.reason: This safety predicate decides whether series data gets deleted.
focus: It cannot see open appenders whose ID is at or below the watermark (see truncateSelectedSeries)

units.summary: Generalized from truncateStaleSeries. It takes a predicate, passes it to gcSeries, and now returns the count of deleted series. Locking, the wait for pending readers, and the WAL tombstone logic are unchanged.
units.headline: Generalize stale truncation into predicate-driven truncateSeries
units.reason: This is the core eviction path, now parameterized with a predicate; deleted series are tombstoned in the WAL.
focus: Callers ignore the returned count; check the tombstone records still match the deleted set
